signals.problem: Freelancers on Saudi platforms (Khamsat, Mostaql) experience buyers delaying payment after work is delivered, and have to rely on platform escrow rules or manual disputes to get paid.
signals.customer: Independent freelancers (مستقلين) selling services on Khamsat/Mostaql or directly to Saudi clients

evidence.claim: A freelancer posted a community question about buyers delaying payment after service completion; platform explains funds auto-release after 72h if buyer doesn't respond.
evidence.source_title: مشاكل تأخر المشتري في الدفع بعد انتهاء الخدمة - مجتمع خمسات
evidence.summary: Per search snippet (WebFetch of the page failed due to proxy error), the thread title and summary indicate a freelancer complaint about buyer payment delay after service delivery; Khamsat's own escrow mechanism auto-releases funds after 72h without buyer action, implying this is a recognized recurring friction point on the platform.

existing_solution.name: Khamsat/Mostaql escrow system
existing_solution.notes: Platform-native escrow with 72h auto-release mitigates but doesn't eliminate the pain for off-platform or direct-client work

signals.workaround: Freelancers rely on platform's built-in escrow/auto-release rules; for off-platform direct clients they have no equivalent protection and must chase payment manually
signals.potential_solution: Lightweight invoicing + automated payment-reminder/escrow-lite tool for Saudi freelancers who work directly with clients (outside Mostaql/Khamsat), integrated with simple ZATCA-compliant invoice generation
signals.business_model: Freemium SaaS, small monthly fee or per-invoice fee
signals.existing_spend: NO RELIABLE EVIDENCE FOUND for direct-client freelancers; on-platform freelancers pay Khamsat/Mostaql commission (not a cash-out fee for this specific pain)
unknowns: How many freelancers work with direct (off-platform) Saudi clients vs exclusively via marketplaces
Whether freelancers would pay for a standalone invoicing/reminder tool vs using free templates
Actual frequency/severity of non-payment for direct-client freelance work in KSA specifically

signals.problem: Holders of the freelance document (وثيقة العمل الحر) are confused about their VAT/ZATCA obligations — when they must register, how to issue a compliant e-invoice, and how e-invoicing (Phase 2) applies to them once income grows.
signals.customer: Freelance-document holders (مستقلين مسجلين بوثيقة العمل الحر) with growing income
signals.source: Vendor blog content explaining freelance-document + VAT + e-invoicing rules; ZATCA official pages

evidence.claim: VAT registration is mandatory above 375,000 SAR/year revenue and optional between 187,500–375,000 SAR; a freelance document does not itself satisfy tax-invoice requirements — separate VAT registration and ZATCA e-invoicing integration are needed.
evidence.source_title: وثيقة العمل الحر في السعودية: دليل شامل - برنامج الفاتورة الإلكترونية
evidence.summary: Per search snippet: explains the gap between having a freelance document and being VAT/e-invoicing compliant, implying freelancers need external guidance/tools to become compliant as income rises.

evidence.claim: ZATCA provides official e-invoicing guidance pages, and multiple third-party 'ZATCA invoice generator' tools exist commercially.
evidence.source_title: فاتورة زاتكا — ZATCA Phase-2 Invoice Generator | arabtoolbox
evidence.summary: Existence of a dedicated commercial ZATCA-compliant invoice generator tool is indirect evidence that individuals/small freelancers need help producing compliant invoices without full accounting software.

existing_solution.name: fawtar.app
existing_solution.notes: Blog + implied product targeting freelance-document holders needing compliant invoices

existing_solution.name: arabtoolbox ZATCA invoice generator
existing_solution.notes: Simple generator tool, suggests low-cost tooling already being built for this niche

signals.workaround: Freelancers read blog guides, use free/generic invoice templates, or under-report to avoid VAT registration complexity
signals.potential_solution: Super-simple guided web app: freelancer enters income, tool tells them if/when they must register for VAT, auto-generates ZATCA-compliant invoices, and reminds them of thresholds — positioned specifically for solo freelance-document holders (not full accounting suites like Qoyod)
signals.business_model: Low monthly subscription (cheaper than full accounting software) or pay-per-invoice
signals.existing_spend: NO RELIABLE EVIDENCE FOUND on specific pricing individuals pay, but existence of dedicated tools (fawtar.app, arabtoolbox) is indirect evidence of a paid niche
unknowns: Real pricing of fawtar.app / competitor tools and whether target segment already finds them adequate
Size of the freelance-document holder population near/above VAT thresholds
Whether ZATCA has simplified this for micro-freelancers, reducing the pain

signals.customer: Small business owners (محلات، مشاريع صغيرة) without dedicated accounting staff

evidence.claim: Many small businesses lack a specialized accountant and find accounting software complex; late invoice recording and tax errors complicate data preparation.

evidence.claim: Businesses risk fines if not properly integrated with ZATCA e-invoicing Phase 2 requirements.
evidence.source_title: الفاتورة الإلكترونية بالسعودية وكيفية الربط لتفادي الغرامة
evidence.summary: Article specifically framed around avoiding ZATCA fines through proper e-invoicing integration, indicating compliance risk is a live concern for businesses in 2026.

existing_solution.name: Qoyod
existing_solution.notes: Established Saudi cloud accounting SaaS targeting SMEs — direct competitor with existing paying customers

signals.workaround: Owners use spreadsheets, hire part-time bookkeepers, or adopt full accounting suites that may be overkill/costly for a tiny shop
signals.potential_solution: Ultra-simple, cheap ZATCA-compliant invoicing+bookkeeping micro-tool for single-owner shops (not full ERP/accounting suite) — narrower and cheaper than Qoyod
signals.business_model: Low monthly SaaS fee (undercutting incumbents) or freemium with paid ZATCA integration
signals.existing_spend: NO RELIABLE EVIDENCE FOUND on exact Qoyod/aamalsoft pricing seen in this session, but their existence as commercial products is proof SMEs already pay for this category
unknowns: Actual price points and market share of Qoyod/aamalsoft among micro-businesses
Whether a solo founder can realistically compete on price/features against funded incumbents

signals.problem: Employees and employers frequently dispute end-of-service benefit (مكافأة نهاية الخدمة) calculations, partly due to confusion between GOSI contributions and the employer-paid gratuity, which are separate but co-occurring obligations.
signals.source: HR SaaS blogs (Bayzat, ZenHR, Jisr) explaining end-of-service calculation and GOSI

evidence.claim: End-of-service benefit is calculated per Article 84: half-month salary per year for the first 5 years, then full-month salary per year after, and this is a common source of disputes because it's separate from but co-occurs with GOSI contributions.
evidence.source_title: كيفية حساب مكافأة نهاية الخدمة في السعودية وفق نظام العمل - بيزات
evidence.summary: Per search-generated summary of multiple HR blog sources, explains the legal formula and flags the GOSI/gratuity distinction as a frequent point of confusion/dispute for employees.

evidence.claim: Multiple free online 'end-of-service calculators' exist (Jisr, ZenHR, tryadel, wazaeef) specifically to help employees estimate what they're owed.
evidence.summary: Existence of several independent free calculator tools from HR software vendors is indirect evidence that individual employees actively search for help calculating what they are legally owed.

existing_solution.name: Jisr / ZenHR / Bayzat end-of-service calculators
existing_solution.notes: Free calculators already exist as lead-gen tools for B2B HR SaaS, not standalone paid consumer products

existing_solution.name: GOSI official FAQ
existing_solution.notes: Official but generic FAQ, not personalized dispute help

signals.workaround: Employees use free calculators or ask HRSD/labor lawyers when they suspect underpayment
signals.potential_solution: Personalized end-of-service dispute-check tool: employee uploads contract/salary history, tool flags discrepancies vs legal formula and generates a ready HRSD complaint draft — monetized via one-off fee only when a discrepancy is found
signals.business_model: One-time fee per report / contingency-style pricing
signals.existing_spend: NO RELIABLE EVIDENCE FOUND (existing calculators are free lead-gen tools, not paid products)
unknowns: Whether individuals would pay for a one-off dispute-check vs use free calculators/lawyers
Volume of actual underpayment disputes vs simple confusion resolved by free tools
Legal complexity of generating HRSD-ready complaint documents without legal liability

evidence.summary: Official FAQ (per search snippet) confirms a defined but multi-step delay/remedy process, implying friction that families need help understanding.
